preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner to call sumTheBounsPool()
Contract must have sufficient token balance to populate the bonus pool
bounsTime must be set and current time must be >= bounsTime for receiveBounsToken to work

violation_target.exploit_hint: 1. Ensure attacker is contract owner. 2. Call sumTheBounsPool(yesToday, twoYesToday) to move half of contract's token balance into dayPoolBouns. 3. Meet bonus requirements (hold minBounsJoin tokens, no sell records). 4. Call receiveBounsToken() to claim bonus rewards from the pool. 5. Verify attacker's token balance increased from the bonus distribution. The owner can manipulate when and how much goes into the bonus pool, potentially claiming disproportionate rewards or locking funds from legitimate users.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The LoveDoge contract has an owner privilege abuse vulnerability in its bonus distribution system. The owner can call sumTheBounsPool() to move half of the contract's token balance into the dayPoolBouns mapping. Then, any user (including the owner/attacker) who meets the requirements can call receiveBounsToken() to claim rewards from this pool. The owner can manipulate when the pool is funded and claim disproportionate rewards before legitimate users.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank(). 2. Transfer tokens to the contract to ensure it has balance for the bonus pool. 3. Call sumTheBounsPool() as owner to populate dayPoolBouns with contract tokens. 4. Call receiveBounsToken() as attacker to claim bonus rewards. 5. Verify attacker's balance increased from the bonus distribution.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Cast the target contract to interface IMyCoinToken. 2. Get the owner address from the contract. 3. Deal tokens to attacker (need minBounsJoin = 100000000000 * 10^9). 4. Deal tokens to contract to fund the bonus pool. 5. Transfer tokens from attacker to contract (as admin, no fees). 6. Impersonate owner and call sumTheBounsPool with date strings from getDays(). 7. Call receiveBounsToken() as attacker. 8. Assert attacker balance increased.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The exploit logic was correct but the token flow was wrong. I should NOT transfer tokens from attacker to contract. Instead, I should deal tokens directly to the contract for the bonus pool, while attacker holds tokens separately to meet minBounsJoin requirement. This way attacker only GAINS from the bonus without losing any tokens.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Deal tokens to attacker (at least minBounsJoin = 1e20). 2. Deal tokens directly to contract (for bonus pool funding). 3. Owner calls sumTheBounsPool to populate dayPoolBouns. 4. Warp time past bounsTime. 5. Attacker calls receiveBounsToken() to claim bonus. 6. Attacker balance increases without any outgoing transfer.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Remove the attacker->contract transfer. 2. Deal tokens directly to contract using deal() cheatcode. 3. Keep attacker balance intact. 4. Owner populates bonus pool. 5. Attacker claims bonus. 6. Assert balance increased.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because I transferred tokens FROM attacker TO contract, which reduced attacker's balance. The bonus received (2.592e17) was much smaller than the tokens transferred out (~1e20), resulting in a net LOSS. The attacker's final balance (9.002e20) was less than initial (1e21).
